args.reason: known-plaintext work is trivial: one known plaintext/ciphertext pair recovers the whole 32-bit key in about 2^10 trials, because the round-robin schedule k(i)=K[i mod 4] plus zero-predecessor forward chaining makes ciphertext byte i depend only on bytes 0..i and key bytes k0..ki
args.detail: Program E = R7 . Xk . Ak . R5 . Cx . A151 . X90 . C+ . R3 . Ak . Xk with b_-1=0. Byte 0 has no cross-byte input at any stage (both C+ and Cx start from the zero predecessor), so ct[0] is a bijection of pt[0] and k0 alone: at most 256 trials fix k0. With k0 known, byte 1 depends only on k0, k1 and the already-known byte 0, so 256 trials fix k1; then k2 and k3 likewise. Total ~4*256 = 2^10 work for the entire key from a single known pair, against the stated key_bits=32 exhaustive bound. Chaining propagates forward only and the key schedule never mixes key bytes, so the non-affine carries give no protection against this sequential per-byte recovery. Not byte-local and not affine, but the known-plaintext attack is trivial, so per charter it cannot be published.
